newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bullion prices dip on profit-taking, tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Japan bullion prices dip on profit-taking, tax rise.

text.p: Gold bullion prices in the Tokyo spot market have fallen since the start of April, as higher yen-based retail prices spurred profit-taking and a sales tax increase on April 1 dampened demand, traders said on Friday.

Bullion prices in the Tokyo spot market, or loco Tokyo, tumbled to nearly flat to world benchmark London, or loco London, as of Friday, compared with a premium of about 120 cents an ounce at the end of March, the traders said.
"Since the start of April, profit-taking has increased in reaction to the rise in yen-based retail prices, which have also dampened fresh gold demand," an official of a major bullion house said.
The yen's recent slip against the dollar boosted yen-based gold retail prices.

"Profit-taking tends to gather steam when retail prices reach about 1,450 yen per gram," another trader said. Yen-based gold retail prices were quoted at 1,456 yen per gram on Friday, up from 1,370 yen at the beginning of January.
Also weighing on physical gold demand in Japan was an increase in the sales tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Investors were active buyers of gold ahead of the tax increase, although demand dried up after it was implemented, traders said..
